grid-tilesize-overlap-2026-08-18: Post-hoc (E41-class) 2x2 tile-size x overlap grid, proposer stage only, consensus-only aggregation, 10 passes per cell, one configuration throughout (detect_brief-text, gemini-3-flash-preview, MINIMAL, T=0.7; 30,130 calls, $18.53 billed). Scored on the four-way tile-union intersection carried on the era-2-487 grid (487 carrier tiles, 20 m buffer), with the preregistered 20 m within-pass deduplication applied to every pass so denser tilings are not penalised for cross-tile duplicates. Best cell per configuration at K=10: 512 px / 12.5 % F1 0.6845 [0.6336,0.7313] MCC 0.5431; 512 px / 50 % F1 0.7611 [0.7126,0.8023] MCC 0.5853; 384 px / 12.5 % F1 0.6574 [0.6038,0.7056] MCC 0.3066; 384 px / 50 % F1 0.7293 [0.6841,0.7686] MCC 0.4909. TWO STANDING PRIORS OVERTURNED. (1) 512 px wins at every overlap and every K, so the 384 px sweet spot does NOT reproduce under one footprint at T=0.7: tile-size effect -0.0803 at 12.5 % [-0.1236,-0.0394] and -0.0976 at 50 % [-0.1206,-0.0752], both excluding zero. (2) Passes do NOT substitute for overlap: 384 px / 12.5 % at K=10 loses to 512 px / 50 % at K=3 by 0.0304 union recall and 0.0926 best F1, at lower cost. NOTE THE SIGN ON OVERLAP: the paired contrasts are computed on run-averaged single-pass per-tile counts with NO consensus filter, so (12.5 % - 50 %) = +0.1207 at 512 px and +0.1381 at 384 px means 50 % overlap COSTS about 0.12-0.14 F1 at a single pass. Overlap reverses and becomes the most valuable factor in the grid only once the corroboration filter it creates is switched on -- which is why the best cell is a 50 % one. Tile size never reverses. The interaction is UNRESOLVED: difference-of-differences -0.0173 [-0.0580,+0.0248], p=0.4033, spanning zero. ALL OF THIS IS CONDITIONAL ON THE ABSENCE OF A PRECISION STAGE: no verifier has run over any grid cell, so whether the tile-size ranking and the overlap effect survive verification is untested (recall-levers programme Phase 1, $6.33). Bootstrap intervals here are at B=10,000 per the 2026-08-19 PI ruling (erratum E82), not the 1,000 Decision 10 pre-specified; the paired contrasts use the analysis script's own resampler, which was never on the D15 defective path, so re-running them at 10,000 moved every delta by 0.00000, every CI width by under 5 %, and no significance verdict. Two of 228 swept cells have an undefined tile MCC, reported as null and never as 0.0 (E81). Artefacts: results/grid-2026-08-18/{grid_analysis.json,sweep.csv,findings.md} and the four per-cell evaluations under results/grid-2026-08-18/conditions/; scripts grid_prepare_scoring.py, grid_analysis.py, grid_materialise_conditions.py.

Best per cell (best-F1@20m; BCa CI95 at B=10,000): 384/50 p>=0.15 k>=10 F1 0.9017 [0.8727,0.9244] MCC 0.8037; 512/50 p>=0.15 k>=9 F1 0.8870 [0.8583,0.9118] MCC 0.8087; 384/12.5 p>=0.15 k>=7 F1 0.8761 MCC 0.7852 (the registered condition keeps p>=0.20 k>=7: F1 0.8752 [0.8424,0.9017] MCC 0.7852); 512/12.5 p>=0.15 k>=5 F1 0.8368 [0.7995,0.8676] MCC 0.8011. BOTH QUESTIONS THE CONSENSUS-ONLY BOARD LEFT OPEN ARE SETTLED, THE SECOND AT 512 PX ONLY. (1) The tile-size ranking REVERSES under the full pipeline: (384-512) = +0.0393 [+0.0052,+0.0741] p=0.0266 at 12.5% overlap — excluding zero on the OPPOSITE side of the consensus-only -0.0803 — and +0.0147 [-0.0095,+0.0394] p=0.2454 at 50% (sign reversed, unresolved). The consensus-only '512 px challenge' to the study's 384 px preference was a truncated-pipeline artefact: the verifier recovers the precision 384 px lacked, while the 384 px cells' higher union-recall ceilings (0.9112/0.9696 vs 0.8879/0.9603) are the resource a verifier cannot create — the Obs 352 rescue mechanism at a new tile-size pair. (2) The overlap reversal SURVIVES the verifier at 512 px but FAILS at 384 px: 50% wins significantly at 512 px ((12.5-50) = -0.0502 [-0.0778,-0.0224] p=0.0003) but not at 384 px (-0.0256 [-0.0517,+0.0001] p=0.0541, the interval reaching +0.0001), at roughly HALF the consensus-only margin — the corroboration filter and the verifier are partially redundant, and the surviving advantage tracks the recall-ceiling edge, as the findings doc predicted. Interaction unresolved (-0.0246 [-0.0613,+0.0114], p=0.1831). CONSENSUS AND VERIFIER ARE COMPLEMENTS, NOT SUBSTITUTES: every cell's best operating point retains a vote threshold (k>=5..10) atop the probability threshold; the pure-verifier k=1 board tops out at 0.8187 (384/12.5) and trails the stacked optimum in every cell by 0.057-0.207. The 384 px tile-MCC saturation pathology dissolves post-verifier (all four cells MCC 0.785-0.809; F1 and MCC rankings broadly agree). Verifier gain over the consensus-only board +0.126..+0.219 best-F1, largest where consensus-only was worst (the 384 px cells). GATES, all passed: exact union-count reproduction at materialisation (stop rule); contiguous candidate-key join; carrier-tile reassignment after the CRS round-trip; each unthresholded union re-scores to its committed sweep row (<=1e-6); each materialised condition reproduces its sweep F1 to <=5e-5 at B=10,000. The paired tile-bootstrap contrasts are the significance instrument (Decision 10 resampler, B=10,000 per E82, seed 42, integer per-tile counts of each single verified set); per-cell CIs are register metadata. Best-F1 operating points are selected on the same ground truth they are scored on, as on the consensus board (E41-class calibration caveat). The tie is not flat on every axis: 3.8 buys +0.0139 of tile-MCC over 3.7 (0.8331 vs 0.8192) while losing 0.0006 of F1, precision-led as its point implies. E3 is FALSIFIED in the opposite direction — 76 thinking tokens per candidate in the verifier seat against the 3.7 verifier's 106, and only 1.1x in the proposer probe (307 vs 275 t/tile), so 'newer' bought LESS thinking, not more. k-ladder-2026-09-12: The pass-count ladder K at otherwise fixed parameters, on 23 ladders: the gold-standard stride A ladder (the only one whose every rung is an exact re-verification of its own first-N union), the thirteen Gemini 3 pv-diag-384 families and the 3.7 gold-standard text screen that Phase 2 completed to four rungs for US$24.8065, the grid 384 px / 50 % MINIMAL text ladder tier E completed for US$4.9595, and the seven 55-map deployment ladders. SHAPE: the return is FRONT-LOADED and K = 3 is on the efficient set of every ladder in the corpus — 37 % to 93 % of a ladder's total F1 gain for 31 % to 64 % of its top rung's cost — while the last step is the worst buy on every ladder, at about US$0.20 to US$27 per 0.001 F1 (the 3.7 family's K = 5 -> K = 10 step buys +0.0004 F1@20 for US$8.68, about US$22 per 0.001 F1). WHAT GOVERNS THE RETURN: the proposer's thinking level, and within a level its temperature. The K = 1 -> best-rung F1 gain is significant on 7 of 7 HIGH-thinking ladders and 2 of 6 MINIMAL ones; four ladders, every one of them MINIMAL, greedy-clique into a SINGLE tier in which K buys nothing detectable; and on both HIGH tracks the gain rises monotonically with temperature (text +0.0559 -> +0.0735 -> +0.0955, image +0.0780 -> +0.0959 -> +0.1514 across T 0.3 -> 0.7 -> 1.0). Read as the diversity dividend (Obs 141) measured on a K ladder: K buys sampling diversity, and pays in proportion to how much the configuration already generates. TILE-MCC DOES NOT FOLLOW F1. Across the 15 verified ladders with an interpretable tile-MCC, F1 rises on all 15 and tile-MCC falls on 10, and NO ladder shows a significant tile-MCC RISE; the gold-standard ladder's +0.0131, § 4 of the findings' one apparent counter-example, tests at BH p = 0.7633. Significant FALLS are found on four ladders — the 3.7-verifier stride B (-0.0112), 3.7 arm 1 (-0.0099), 3.7 arm 2 (-0.0275) and HIGH image T 1.0 (-0.0637, BH p = 0.0420, the family with the largest F1 gain). More passes buy localisation inside already-positive tiles, not tile-level discrimination, which matters for any application whose unit is the tile rather than the mound. CAVEAT on the MCC column: tile-MCC is computed by a string join on source_tile, and three cells of the 3.7 gold-standard text family are scored on a frame whose tile vocabulary is not their proposer's, so their tile-MCC is WITHHELD with a named reason rather than reported (g37-text-k1-verified-opmax, g37-text-k1-verified-carried-p0.10-k1, g37-text-k3-verified-opmax; no raw value is now recorded). The corpus-wide exposure is measured at 3 of 149 committed cells the Era-2 board reads, no published board MCC is affected, and the repair is a corpus-wide decision with the PI because the 384 px frames overlap (reports/tile-mcc-geometric-join-2026-09-12.md). Their F1 is sound and is reported in full. INSTRUMENT (PI ruling): the board's round-robin tile-swap micro-F1 permutation is THE instrument — 10,000 permutations, seed 42, BH q = 0.05 within each ladder's own round-robin, tile-MCC swapped on byte-identical masks so a ΔF1 and a ΔMCC are two statistics of one permutation — and the registered per-map paired sign-swap is the CROSS-CHECK. Where both cover a pair (8 pairs, 2 ladders) all eight tile-MCC significance calls AGREE, with ΔMCC estimates within 0.0006; one marginal F1 call differs (stride A's K = 3 -> 5, BH p 0.0079 against 0.0655), so the instrument choice is live for marginal F1 claims and immaterial to the MCC conclusion. THE TWO CORPORA AGREE once resolution is accounted for. The deployment MINIMAL ladders' own cells, scored on random 487-tile subsets of their own 8,541 tiles (200 draws, seed 42, same instrument), keep BH significance in 197 of 200 draws at ΔF1 +0.0547 and in only 39 of 200 at +0.0192 — a subsampling standard deviation of ~0.0114 either way — so 487 tiles resolve a ΔF1 of about 0.03 and above and not below. The nine MINIMAL ladders sort by effect size rather than by corpus (every one at or above +0.0546 separates, every one at or below +0.0223 does not), and the deployment range +0.0192..+0.0547 sits INSIDE the gold-standard range +0.0139..+0.0600. So 'K buys nothing detectable' on four MINIMAL configurations is a statement about 487 tiles, not about K. PARETO MCC SET: on tile-MCC no rung above K = 1 is ever the admissible choice — K = 1 holds the highest tile-MCC on 8 of the 15 interpretable ladders and is never significantly beaten on it — so the MCC-efficient rung is K = 1 wherever tile-level discrimination is the objective, while the F1-efficient rung is K = 3. The two objectives select different rungs, and that is the review's practical finding. A GEOMETRY EFFECT, consensus-only: at fixed MINIMAL text T 0.7 the grid study's K = 1 -> 10 gain is about 2.2x larger at 12.5 % overlap than at 50 % (+0.1441 against +0.0660 at 384 px; +0.0947 against +0.0425 at 512 px), and tile-MCC RISES with K on all four consensus-only cells (+0.029..+0.132) — the opposite of the verified ladders, consistent with the same mechanism. Overlap and pass count buy the same redundancy. The pattern does not survive to the verified deployment ladders, which order the other way. THE VERIFIER STAGE REVERSES tile-MCC's RESPONSE TO K, and absorbs about 60 % of K's F1 return (§ 8.6, added on the PI's ruling 2026-09-13). On ONE pool and ONE geometry — the grid study's 384 px / 50 % B-geometry MINIMAL text pool, which is the deployment stride-B tiling at gold-standard scale — K = 1 -> 10 raises F1@20 by +0.0660 with tile-MCC RISING +0.0444 consensus-only (results/grid-2026-08-18/sweep.csv, cell g384_ov192, best F1@20 per K over the corroboration x vote grid: 0.6633/0.4465 at K = 1, 0.7293/0.4909 at K = 10), and raises F1@20 by only +0.0262 with tile-MCC FALLING -0.0238 once the same pool is verified (tier-e/ladder.json and each rung's evaluation: 0.8680/0.8211 at K = 1, 0.8942/0.7973 at K = 10). So the verifier takes 60.3 % of what extra passes buy on F1 — because it was already removing much of what extra passes remove — and turns a tile-level GAIN into a tile-level LOSS, a swing of 0.0682 MCC. This is the mechanism of the TILE-MCC DOES NOT FOLLOW F1 finding above measured directly rather than inferred: tile-MCC's response to K is a property of the PIPELINE STAGE, not of K. Its limits are stated with it: one geometry, one thinking level, one temperature, one modality, one corpus, and the ladder's own DMCC steps are not individually significant (tile-MCC separates on none of its six pairs), so the claim is about the sign and size of the shift BETWEEN stages. NOT CLAIMED: no MCC RANKING of rungs, tiering stays on the preregistered F1; and the five non-separating ladders' MCC moves are not shown to be zero. ON THE LAST STEP: NO ladder's F1-admissible set excludes K = 10 — all twenty ladders that have a K = 10 rung admit it — so the top rung is never statistically ruled out, only never worth its price, which is the formal counterpart of the US$1,100-to-US$43,000 per 0.001 F1 figures above. ON THE TWO OBJECTIVES: K = 1 is ruled out on F1 on 20 of 22 ladders and is admissible on tile-MCC on 22 of 22, holding the highest tile-MCC on 13 of them, so the PARETO MCC SET claim above now rests on the canonical simultaneous instrument rather than on a pairwise count.
